note: Every rule cites a clause checked against a primary source or taken from a compiled control taxonomy built from the framework documents. Unverified instruments are listed under 'pending' and produce no findings. Model inference counts as processing: prompts, retrieved context, and tool results are all data sent to wherever the model runs.

rules.title: Level 3/4 or personal data processed outside Kuwait
rules.finding: CITRA's framework requires subscribers of cloud services, private companies included, to ensure that Level 3 and 4 data, and personal data of individuals of the kinds listed in §4.1.4 (identification, contact, behavioural and other personal data), is not hosted or stored outside Kuwait 'for any purpose, or in any form, whether temporarily or permanently'. Sending this data to a model outside Kuwait for inference falls inside that wording. The framework is not consistent here: §3.2.1.2.2, the duty for private companies, bars only personal data at Level 3 or 4, while §4.2.1.1.3 bars personal data generally. This tool takes the stricter reading; under the narrower one, Level 2 personal data (names, contact details, civil ID) could be hosted abroad. Confirm with counsel which reading applies before relying on either.
rules.remediation: Run inference in Kuwait (in-country licensed cloud or on-premises), or keep Level 3/4 and personal data out of the agent's reach entirely.

rules.title: Level 2 data on a public cloud outside Kuwait
rules.finding: CITRA permits Level 2 data on public cloud if it meets encryption requirements with keys held only by the customer. Model inference needs the data in plaintext at the provider, so customer-held keys protect storage but not inference.
rules.remediation: Document that inference plaintext exposure is accepted for Level 2 data, or move inference in-country.

sources.instrument: CITRA Cloud Computing Regulatory Framework (Resolution 112 of 2021)

rules.title: Cloud provider must be CITRA-licensed
rules.finding: Shared content may only go to public, hybrid, or community cloud providers registered and licensed by CITRA. A model vendor's API is a cloud service for this purpose. A private cloud dedicated to the organisation is outside this clause.
rules.remediation: Confirm the model provider (or the cloud hosting it) is CITRA-licensed before go-live.

sources.instrument: CITRA Cloud Computing Regulatory Framework (Resolution 112 of 2021)

rules.title: Only non-sensitive metadata may leave Kuwait
rules.finding: Residency rules cover customer content; operational metadata may be processed globally only if it stays non-sensitive. Vendor telemetry, abuse monitoring, and logging can carry prompt content out of the country.
rules.remediation: Confirm the vendor's telemetry, abuse-monitoring, and log retention stay in-country or exclude prompt and response content.

rules.title: CBK approval needed before signing a cloud outsourcing agreement for the model
rules.finding: A model vendor's API, a hyperscaler-hosted model, or a hybrid cloud is a public, community, or hybrid cloud service under CORF. Where it interacts with systems holding sensitive data (customer, financial, transactional), the bank must seek CBK approval at least one month before signing the agreement, submitting the scope, risk assessment, data storage location, the provider's controls and audit reports, and proposed service levels. The cloud risk assessment must cover location and data residency.
rules.remediation: Submit the CBK approval request at least one month before contract signature, with the items CORF lists, and record hosting location and residency in the cloud risk assessment.

sources.instrument: CBK Cyber and Operational Resilience Framework (CORF) v1.0, December 2025

rules.title: CBK approval needed before an AI system goes live
rules.finding: CORF names artificial intelligence and machine learning as emerging technologies. A CBK-regulated entity must seek CBK approval at least one month before go-live, outlining the technology, how it is applied, the risk assessment results, and the risk response. This applies wherever the model is hosted, including on-premises.
rules.remediation: Submit the approval request at least one month before go-live. This assessment's threat register, residency findings, and path to Go can support the risk assessment and risk response sections.

sources.instrument: CBK Cyber and Operational Resilience Framework (CORF) v1.0, December 2025

rules.title: Saudi personal data transferred outside the Kingdom
rules.finding: Every inference call is a cross-border transfer of the personal data in the prompt. It needs an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards, limited to the minimum necessary data. Continuous transfers of sensitive data also need a written risk assessment.
rules.remediation: Establish the transfer basis (adequacy or SCCs/BCRs), minimise personal data in prompts, and complete the transfer risk assessment before go-live.

rules.title: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles apply
rules.finding: SDAIA's AI Ethics Principles apply to entities developing or deploying AI in the Kingdom, covering accountability, transparency, privacy and security, and human oversight across the lifecycle.
rules.remediation: Map the deployment to the principles; the per-action audit log and human-approval evidence from this assessment support accountability and transparency.

rules.title: Government use of generative AI
rules.finding: SDAIA's Generative AI Guidelines for Government set expectations for government entities adopting generative AI. Non-binding, but reviewers will expect alignment.
rules.remediation: Reference the guidelines in the deployment's governance pack.

sources.instrument: SDAIA Generative AI Guidelines for Government (January 2024)

rules.title: UAE personal data transferred outside the UAE
rules.finding: Inference outside the UAE transfers personal data cross-border. It must go to a jurisdiction with adequate protection, or meet one of the conditions for transfer without adequacy.
rules.remediation: Confirm the hosting country's adequacy status or document the Art. 23 condition relied on.

rules.title: DIFC Regulation 10 — personal data in AI systems
rules.finding: Processing personal data through an autonomous or semi-autonomous system brings Regulation 10 obligations. The deployer carries controller-equivalent accountability, and affected individuals must get clear notice that an AI system is processing their data.
rules.remediation: Issue the Regulation 10 transparency notice and record deployer / operator responsibilities in the contract with the model provider.

rules.title: Qatar personal data processed outside Qatar
rules.finding: Cross-border flow of personal data is regulated under Qatar's PDPPL, and inference outside Qatar is such a flow.
rules.remediation: Document the lawful basis for the cross-border flow and confirm it is not restricted.

rules.title: NCSA secure AI adoption guidelines
rules.finding: NCSA's Guidelines for Secure Adoption and Usage of AI (v1.0, 2024) are voluntary, but give Qatari reviewers a reference for AI lifecycle security, governance, and testing.
rules.remediation: Align the red-team and monitoring controls in this report with the guidelines.
